comment: The oldest systems each part of an OXT-Beyond package must run on, as README.md documents them. platform_matrix.py reads it for the package checks of the build workflows (the ELF and Mach-O floor checks and the extension library check, with --matrix), and tests/test_platform_matrix.py checks that README.md still states every floor here. Change a floor here and in README.md together. An exception is a part that is known to need more than its platform's floor; it names the files, the floor they need instead, and why, so it shows in every log and fails once those files are gone.

mac-universal.description: macOS IDE, one app for Apple Silicon and Intel
readme: macOS 11 or later on Apple Silicon, 10.13 or later on Intel

extensions.description: native libraries of the bundled xTalk Suite extensions (Contents/Tools/Extensions/*/code/universal-mac)
readme: native libraries built for macOS 10.15 Catalina on Intel and macOS 11 on Apple Silicon
Linux x86-64 with glibc 2.31 or later

linux-arm64.description: Linux IDE, 64-bit ARM, without the browser widget
readme: 64-bit ARM Linux with glibc 2.31 or later

linux-x86.description: Linux 32-bit x86 standalones (the runtime every Linux and Windows package carries)

web.description: Web engine and web IDE: Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, with the capability differences BUILDING.md lists

android.description: Android standalone runtime: carried over unchanged from oxt-runtimes-1.15, not built or checked here

linux_exceptions.comment: Parts every Linux package carries (the 32-bit x86 extension libraries that x86 standalones get) that need more than the package's own floor. Each applies to every linux-* platform; a pattern that matches no file in the package fails the check, since the exception no longer describes anything.
